rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice: use it before a mass noun for the smallest amount and before a count noun for the fewest.

example.english: This gift costs at least three hundred dollars to buy.
example.traditional: 呢份禮物最少要三百蚊先買到。
example.jyutping: ni1 fan6 lai5 mat6 zeoi3 siu2 jiu3 saam1 baak3 man1 sin1 maai5 dou2

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice when “least” refers to the smallest amount or frequency, as in practising the least.

example.english: I practise the least out of everyone.
example.traditional: 成班人入面，我最少練習。
example.jyutping: seng4 baan1 jan4 jap6 min6 ngo5 zeoi3 siu2 lin6 zaap6

rows.note: Use this when “least” means the lowest degree of a gradable adjective, such as “least happy” or “least likely,” rather than the smallest amount.

example.english: I was the least happy on this trip.
example.traditional: 今次旅行入面，我最唔開心。
example.jyutping: gam1 ci3 leoi5 hang4 jap6 min6 ngo5 zeoi3 m4 hoi1 sam1
